w: A kishore (teenage devotee) asked Swamishri, "Swami, do you have any advice or suggestion for me?" Swamishri replied, "Say the rosary, do bhajan, study hard and don’t smoke or get into any addictions."

I am Sevak When the car stopped at the cottage, Swamishri unbuckled his seatbelt. The youth driving the car said, "I would have unbuckled it for you. There was no need to do it yourself." Swamishri replied, "Sometimes one has to become a 'svayam-sevak' (one's own servant)." The youth responded, "There is no need for you to be svayam-sevak. You are the boss!" Swamishri, placing a finger on his chest, said, "I am not boss. I am 'sevak' (servant)." Despite being the guru of hundreds of thousands, Swamishri always harbors the feeling of sevakbhav and whenever any occasion permits his virtue of servitude is revealed.

Inclination for Bhajan In the evening, Swamishri arrived on time at 7.10 pm for the children's assembly. But not a single child was present. The compere apologized, saying, "Swami I am sorry, you have arrived but the children have not. What shall we do till then?" Swamishri naturally replied, "There's nothing to worry. We will do bhajan." With no trace of disturbance or agitation on his face, Swamishri's inclination for bhajan is an ongoing agenda.
Strive to earn according to one's needs but don't take giant strides. On doing more than one's needs, one then fails to worship God.
Progress means offering devotion to God and expelling lust, anger, greed and base instincts. Otherwise, there is darkness.
Even a little refuge (ashro) in God, Satsang and righteous living will save you from any powerful enticement.
Faith in God and good character will help accomplish any work.
We fold our hands at the arrival of the father-in-law and son-in-law, then should we not do likewise to God who has given us this human body!

Swamishri celebrated the 4th BAPS mandir inauguration anniversary (patotsav) with Vedic rites. Thereafter, an assembly commenced with bhajans and speeches by sadhus and finally concluded with Swamishri's blessings.
In the evening assembly a kirtan-bhakti program was performed by sadhus. Thereafter a speech by Viveksagar Swami and blessings from Swamishri enthused the devotees.

Kishore - Kishori Din In the evening Kishore Day assembly a newsdesk was set up – called BAPS News West. The channel reporter visited the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir and posed a question about the need for a mandir. Vishvamurti Swami answered the question. Then the reporter asked Viveksagar Swami about Swamishri’s life and work. Then the newsdesk presented inspiring stories from the lives of devotees. Then the newsdesk showed the large fomrat trailor of Mystic India and details about the mandirs in Houston and Chicago. This was followed by an award giving ceremony. Youths dressed as distinguished people felicitated Swamishri with a Ph.D. Then through the Newsdesk presentation, data on Swamishri’s effort in building mandirs was presented. Dr Swami presented the World President Award to Swamishri and then spoke about Swamishri’s greatness. The kishores then performed a traditional colorful dance on the lyric, “Sadgun na bhandar Pramukh Swami…” and finally presented an 84 ft.
After the dignitaries addressed the assembly Swamishri blessed the audience.

The BAPS West youths organized a Kishore/Kishori Din program at the Anaheim Convention center celebrating Swamishri's relentless efforts to enhance society and Satsang. They uniquely described the current and future progress of Satsang due to Swamishri's efforts with a news report from "BAPS News West."

Kishores also presented Swamishri with many awards, such as the "Lifetime Achievement Award" and "Sadhuta Award". Real-life incidents of West region kishores and kishoris who preserved their faith in difficult circumstances were narrated. Kishores performed dances to welcome Swamishri and spark the enthusiasm for the proposed construction of a new temple in Chino Hills.

Senior saints also conveyed their wisdom in the assembly. P. Viveksagar Swami explained the many hardships Swamishri has endured for the constant progress of Satsang and societal work. P. Doctor Swami stated that the roots of peace and happiness lie in God, and to realize God, one must find the true Saint.

Many dignitaries were also present in the assembly. Honorable Judge James Gray of the Superior Court of Orange County presented a plaque to Swamishri for Swamishri's commitment to Hinduism and compassion for humanity. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly elaborating on the four aims of one's life, dharma, artha, kama, and moksha. He explained that one needs dharma in every aspect of one's life. One also needs to acquire the knowledge of atma and Parmatma, which is accomplished through the association of the Saint.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - Swamishri's Compassion for a Child Addicted to Gutkha
w: Whenever his little grandson cried a local man of Bhadra would place a bidi in his mouth. Subsequently, the little child became addicted. Presently, he is three and a half years old and eats two packets of gutkha (tobacco) daily. When he does not get the gutkha he throws a tantrum. The boy's father and grandfather are addicted to gutkha and biddi.

Sometimes, the child goes all by himself to the local shop to get a gutkha under his father's name. The innocent, tender child has become habituated to tobacco all because of his father and grandfather's mistake.

The child's uncle, who became a satsangi in Surat, brought him today before Swamishri for darshan. He placed him on the rostrum. Swamishri welcomed him, "Jai Swaminarayan." But the ignorant little child did not know what to say. He simply looked down and remained quiet. Swamishri asked for a box of prasad, and taking a sweet ball from it, said, "Take this, and don't eat gutkha. Gutkha spoils your body and causes disease. Therefore don't eat it."

Swamishri's compassion for the little, tender child was apparent to all. To release him from the shackles of addiction Swamishri blessed him and advised him and his relatives. All those present witnessed the moments which freed probably the youngest addict in the world from his addiction.

Several teenage satsangi boys had come from Rajkot for Swamishri’s darshan. When Swamishri learnt that they daily clean the mandir he became very happy. Swamishri showered his blessings upon them and said, “Clean the mandir properly and your soul, too, will become pure. Anger and other base instincts will disappear, and you will experience peace within.”

Both father and son complained to Swamishri about each other. The son revealed, “He cannot stop getting angry. He explodes at any time.” The father replied, “It is the same with him!” Swamishri answered, “It is good that both of you have pointed out each other’s failings correctly. Now tell me whom do I have to bless.” “Me,” both father and son replied together. Swamishri happily advised, “Anger damages one’s business, home and everything. Therefore, give it up when you get angry, become alert and start doing bhajan. If you are alert then you will be able to diminish your anger gradually. See how politely and sweetly a businessmen talks in his business. Likewise, talk calmly and you will progress in life.”

Today during a conversation it came up that a parshad, Niranjan Bhagat, is originally from Bhadra. So Pramukh Swami Maharaj found out his father's name and then said, "Your grandfather Mavjibhai was a great devotee. His father Nanjibhai also served Shastriji Maharaj greatly. When Shastriji Maharaj got off at the station, he went with a bullock cart to fetch him. When one bullock ran away, he seated Shastriji Maharaj in the cart, put himself in the place of the bullock and brought him from the station to the village. He did such seva. Your grandfather became a bullock for Shastriji Maharaj. In the same way, we too must become bullocks for Shastriji Maharaj and serve and work."

Swamishri departed from Mumbai in the morning and arrived in Bochasan via Vadodara at 11.30 am. Swamishri was accorded a warm welcome by the devotees.
Swamishri’s compassion

16 June 2009, Mumbai A fallen devotee poured his heart with remorse, “Swami! I had a lot of manushyabhav for you. Because of that I had given up Satsang for eight years. I had stopped coming to the mandir. Subsequently, I was left devastated and miserable. I ask you to have compassion upon me and take me back at your feet.” Swamishri listened with compassion and patience. Once he had finished confessing, Swamishri blessed him by placing his hand on his head and said, “Now forget what has happned. God has blessed you with spiritual awareness. Do satsang regularly. Do not fall into the habit of addictions and vices. And be regular in the Sunday assembly. Maharaj has forgiven you, and you’ll be happy.”
Conviction in god’s doership bestows stability

24 June 2009, Mumbai “In spite of the many difficulties and problems you face how do you maintain patience and equipoise?” a sadhu asked Swamishri. “From the very beginning I believe that Maharaj and Swami are the all-doer. When something happens what can we do? So I have decided from the beginning that God is the all-doer. “One faces problems when one has to deal with others or get things done. In such large organisations there are bound to be problems, but by having faith in God and leaving it upon him, I have experienced that everything works out well. Maharaj, himself, wanted to perform the pratishtha of Gadhada mandir, but he couldn’t do it. So, whatever happens is all due to the wish of God. By leaving everything upon him, there are no problems. One will find people who criticize in whatever one does, but as long as one makes honest efforts with God and his Sadhu in mind, there is no need to worry.”

Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the mandir for the darshan of Thakorji. After lovingly having darshan of Ghanshyam Maharaj, Swamishri came to the central shrine. After having darshan with concentration of the adornment of Thakorji in the central shrine, he stepped back a little and again had darshan of the murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj visible through the doors of the bed chamber, and minutely observed what changes there were in the clothes.
With what devotion and concentration Swamishri does darshan! Swamishri was teaching everyone this way of doing darshan.

Adesh Gupta, owner of Liberty Shoes, came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. His sister had had cancer, and when he had come for Swamishri's darshan at that time, Swamishri had given him a sanctified flower of Thakorji. Taking this flower, his sister went to London for special treatment. When the doctors there examined her, no cancer was found at all! After this astonishing event, Shri Gupta and his family have unique faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

A gentleman named Tripathi came for darshan. He said, "Together with Saurin, the son of Champaklal Sheth, I had much of the company of Yogiji Maharaj. In particular, in Yogiji Maharaj's last days, he had specially called us for seva. We had the privilege of every seva, from washing his dhotis onwards. At the end, Yogiji Maharaj called me and said, 'If you have any difficulty, meet this Pramukh Swami, and your difficulty will be removed.'" Yogiji Maharaj had introduced countless spiritual seekers to Pramukh Swami Maharaj in this way.

In the sadhus' ashram today, to fulfil the devotees' wish, Mahant Swami Maharaj happily made jalebis in the heated ghee. Then he offered the thal before Thakorji. But the paper spread in it had lifted slightly and was getting a little in the way between Thakorji and the jalebis. Swamishri folded it two or three times and set it right.
Should this be called perfection or supreme devotion? Whatever it is called, for us it is something to follow.

Dr Milanbhai Patel had come for Mahant Swami Maharaj's darshan. He asked Swamishri a question that had been playing on his mind for a long time: "All kinds of people come to meet you, so how do you neutralise that energy (remove the effect of that energy)?"
Swamishri said, "There is no need to neutralise it. Bhagwan's power comes from above."
